text: I also wish to thank Mr Murali Pillai for helping me address some of the queries which Member Mr Louis Ng has raised but I do agree it was a bit long  .

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: And to also Member Ms Tin Pei Ling for spearheading the workgroup's public outreach and feedback process.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The policies behind the Bill have gone through rounds of revision, containing the collective wisdom of all Singaporeans and professionals who had given us their views.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Indeed, those in Parliament who have spoken in this debate, they have all unanimously supported the amendment Bill.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I want to thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary Mr Eric Chua, for his support and for his endorsement of our proposals too.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: If the Bill is passed today, the baton will now be handed over to MSF to ensure that the amendments are implemented effectively.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: To be sure, any parent who makes a maintenance application can choose which child or children he wishes to file the application against.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Yet, if I am one of the children at the receiving end of a maintenance claim, the MPA allows me to join my siblings to the application.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: After doing so, those siblings whom I have joined will be co-respondents, and the Tribunal may order any or all of them to contribute maintenance, depending on the facts of the case.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This was built into the Bill right at the beginning of the history of the MPA by then Assoc Prof Walter Woon, who saw that it was not fair that only one child should bear the burden, to the exclusion of others.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mr Don Wee also asked what happens if the parent supported the child for some years but later moved out of the child's life.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: At the leave hearing, the Tribunal will consider the specific facts and the degree of the abandonment, abuse or neglect.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: If the parent is able to show a good reason why he is nevertheless still deserving of maintenance, the Tribunal may allow him to proceed if it is just and equitable.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: And if leave is granted and a maintenance order is eventually made, the quantum will be set at a just amount, taking into account the above factors.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Ms Janet Ang also asked whether other countries have similar legislation.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Not many countries but some of the countries that have it include India, Israel and France.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The issue of destitute parents with children who have means, needs addressing.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We have heard the view that children do not owe anything to their parents since they did not ask to be born.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: These are the cases where the abandonment is the most egregious.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: These parents are left without a roof over their heads and without means of sustenance.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It is time for such children to be called upon to fulfil their obligations.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng was concerned about calling in the children for conciliation when the parents became destitute on account of their own financial mismanagement, or when they previously abused their children.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Likewise, Ms Janet Ang observed that for many destitute parents, it is not the children who have abandoned their parent, but the parent who first walked out of the family.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This does indeed mean that for a good many destitute parents, this amendment will not apply to them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Like the MPA as a whole, it is only for those few cases where it is the children, holding on to the mindset that they owe nothing to those who have tirelessly brought them up and blatantly abandon their parent.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But cases where the parent had cared for the child and later become destitute due to financial mismanagement, they are different.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The parent may have made financial mistakes in the past, but if there was genuine care for the child, then my view is that the child should provide at least some support and there should not be total abandonment of his or her parent.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This amendment will not compel the child to give any particular sum of money.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It only allows the Commissioner to call the child in so that a discussion can take place.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Through such discussion, it could even lead to an improvement in ties between child and parent – and that is something that I hope will, in some cases, happen.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Ms Janet Ang also asked if cases can be initiated by social workers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The MPA does allow applications to be made on the parent's behalf by persons who have the parent's authorisation.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This is for cases where the parent is unable to make his own application due to an infirmity.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Ms Ang also asked if we would consider conciliatory efforts by social service agencies, before the Commissioner reaches out to the children of destitute parents.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This is indeed what our workgroup has recommended.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The Commissioner will only act as a last resort, when the attempts of the welfare homes and social workers to reach out to children do not succeed, or when they cannot be located or contacted.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It is in such cases that the Commissioner's powers of identifying and locating the children for the purposes of conciliation are helpful, and the Commissioner can then call them in to hear their side of the story.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Indeed, if the concern is on conciliatory efforts, there is no better place for this than in the Commissioner's office, given its long history and good track record in terms of resolution rates.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The amendments to prevent the misuse of the Act are certainly timely.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Many of those who responded to our public consultation paper felt that it was about time this issue was looked into, to help what one respondent described as the "broken children trapped within an adult body".

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Their only qualm was that it would not be enough, since only those with official records of abandonment, abuse or neglect will benefit from this amendment.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This is echoed by Mr Louis Ng and Mr Yip Hon Weng in the House today.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I want to assure Members that both the Commissioner and Tribunal are mindful of unreported cases and they will adopt a trauma-informed approach in sensitively supporting them through the whole process.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Where appropriate and with consent, they are also assisted by referrals to help services and counselling so that they can find healing.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: From my own observation of Tribunal proceedings, the Tribunal will hear all parties and consider all circumstances of the case, including the form and extent of abuse or neglect, to determine whether it will be just and equitable for the child to maintain the parent.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Evidence that can be furnished to the Tribunal is not limited to official records.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It can also consist of oral or written recollection of the abuse incidents from the viewpoint of the child.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But the fact remains that where there are no official records, the abuse would be unknown to the Tribunal until it is surfaced by the child.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: In such instances, the child would have to be involved in the hearing.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: And our proposed process to deal with the claim without involving the child will not apply.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: So, we cannot do away with this requirement of official records.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But as society becomes more aware of family violence and more willing to report it, this may benefit more people.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the statistics on the number of instances the law has been unfairly used against the children.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But for the few that do, it certainly makes a big difference for them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Some of the amendments are of the kind that also arise from experience.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The Act, when it was first passed, was to solve the practical problem of maintenance for needy elderly parents.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: That is very much still the core of the Act today, but time and experience have revealed how often this practical problem cannot be resolved in isolation from other issues in the family relationship.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The power to make non-monetary directions is new, but it is one that will be given to a Tribunal that has a long history and experience with adjudicating maintenance cases and well-developed institutional practices.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It is a Tribunal that knows how to use this legislative tool to make families better off.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: With regards to Ms Yeo Wan Ling's query if non-monetary directions could in some sense be introduced at the conciliation stage, the answer is, of course.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: As noted by Ms Yeo herself, the Commissioner is not able to issue orders to the parties as this lies with the Tribunal.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: However, the Commissioner can and does refer the parties for counselling and other social services, with their consent.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The Maintenance of Parents Act is an Act that is enacted for the small category of needy and neglected parents, but in its effect, it touches everyone one way or another because we are the children of parents and many of us are parents ourselves.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: As mentioned by Ms Carrie Tan, many today do not wish to burden their children and will not come to them for help.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Yet, where possible, it is better for the parent to teach their child from young to have a caring heart for the family and by extension, for the wider community.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: To this end, I am in full agreement with the Members who have raised the key focal area of education, like Mr Don Wee and Mr Yip Hon Weng.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Twelve years ago, I led a Working Group comprising about 10 members and we tabled the 2010 Maintenance of Parents (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We introduced the conciliation-first approach to help elderly parents and their children resolve maintenance disputes out of Court.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This was a major change as they used to apply directly to the Tribunal for the Maintenance of the Parents for an order, for their children to pay them maintenance.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This tended to worsen the already strained family ties.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, I formed a nine-member Work Group comprising of Parliamentarians here.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We formed this group more than a year ago and we have completed our deliberations and review.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My Work Group's key thrust is to strike the right balance in strengthening provisions for parents while introducing measures to prevent its misuse.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Second, we propose to put in place new processes to prevent the misuse of the MPA by parents who have abandoned, abused or neglected their children and did not fulfil their parental duties.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In so doing, we also protect and spare their children from unnecessary distress.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We conducted two rounds of public consultation in January and November last year with citizens, stakeholders and professionals from the social and legal sectors.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We also had an online survey as part of our consultative process.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: All said, there was general support for the proposed amendments.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day.
